LESSON: READING 6.2.1 WORD READING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Weather and Our Environment Suggested Vocabulary: sun, shine, rain, clouds, blow
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Word Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Word Reading, part of Weather and Our Environment Suggested Vocabulary: sun, shine, rain, clouds, blow in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we ensure we pronounce words clearly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Word Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learning independently is enhanced as the learner works on their own as they practise reading decodable words.

Values:
Peace: A learner displays tolerance during group and pair work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others to practise reading the words.

Link to other learning areas

Word reading is also emphasised in Kiswahili Language and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards,

• Audio, video clip,

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast.

b) pronounce words with the target

sounds accurately for fluency,


c) value the role of fluency in

lifelong learning.

• Learners are guided to

individually identify words with

the sounds: /f/, /n/ /h/ /ɒ/ and / /

ɔː/.

• Learners with low vision are

guided to select words with the

target sounds from a chart while

learners with blindness to select

words with the target sounds

from a braille chart.

• Learners are guided to

individually read words

including words with target

letter sounds.

• Learners are guided to read

words about weather and the

environment with minimal

hesitations.

• Learners are guided to

individually practise reading

sentences containing decodable

words.
